clue.text: Macbeth struggling to cross two rivers in wee vessel

indicators.note: to cross means the jumbled name spans the rivers, holding them inside
struggling suggests flailing about, so the name Macbeth is jumbled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, and the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A Scottish king battles to ford two rivers in a tiny boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' turns MACBETH into CHAMBET; 'to cross' puts R and PO inside it. 'wee' is Scots for small but also means urine, the joke of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom pot kept for urinating at night is literally a receptacle for wee, the colloquial word for urine.

clue.text: Symbolic systems the end for Pindaric works?

indicators.note: the end for a word is its final letter, here the last letter of Pindaric

parts.note: works here are poems, and Pindar's characteristic works were odes

explanation.surface: A musing on whether elaborate formal systems spell the end of Pindar-style poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Pindar was a Greek poet famous for odes, so 'Pindaric works' reads naturally as a phrase; split it, taking C from the end of 'Pindaric' and ODES from 'works'.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems of symbols standing for words or messages, such as Morse or ciphers, are what we call codes.

clue.text: Six-footer gathering smallest amount is student of structure

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the insect holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an ant is an insect, and insects have six legs or feet
an atom is a tiny particle, a byword for the smallest amount

explanation.surface: An insect collecting the tiniest scrap turns out to be a keen scholar of form.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the study of bodily structure, so one who practises it is a student of how bodies are built.

clue.text: Enemy takes both manoeuvres similarly

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests moving pieces around, so the letters of the first three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military report: the enemy executes both manoeuvres in the same way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' looks like a noun the enemy carries out, but it is a verb acting on 'Enemy takes both'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in the same way or for the same reason, a synonym of similarly.

clue.text: The man to deliver fish brought in

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the fish goes into the word for deliver

parts.note: to rid is to free or deliver someone from something
char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: A man's job is to bring in a delivery of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, as in Richard III; the setter treats any male name as a valid answer to 'The man'.

clue.text: The litres consumed in rounds in the Old Black Ram!

indicators.note: consumed in means swallowed by, so the pieces sit inside the two round letters

parts.note: rounds are circular shapes, each like the letter O
L is the abbreviation for litre, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Pints downed round after round at a pub called the Old Black Ram.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Iago warns Brabantio that 'an old black ram is tupping your white ewe', meaning the Moor of Venice; the pub sign surface hides that line.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago's insulting description of the Moorish general in Shakespeare's tragedy gives the hero's name.

clue.text: Chagall for one has stuff in retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word for stuff is read backwards

parts.note: to cram is to stuff something full

explanation.surface: An artist's retrospective exhibition is crammed with his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospective' suggests the art-show sense, natural with Chagall, but here it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was the Russian-French painter, so he is one example of a man with this first name.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about old dodge

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for enthusiastic goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: avid means keen or enthusiastic

explanation.surface: Someone keen on an old trick or dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to evade or keep clear of it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: One crawling in surrender having tilt with English knight

indicators.note: having means holding within, so the word for surrender contains the other pieces

parts.note: to cede is to give up or surrender
N is the chess notation for a knight
to tip is to tilt

explanation.surface: A craven knight surrenders, tilting with an Englishman in a joust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tilt' and 'knight' evoke jousting, but tilt simply means TIP and knight is the chess letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: A many-legged arthropod that creeps along the ground is a creature that crawls.

clue.text: One offers vision of what may come to pass

definitions.text: One offers vision of what may come to pass

parts.words: One offers vision of what may come to pass
parts.note: sounds like a prophet foreseeing the future, but means a driver's glass showing vehicles behind that may overtake

explanation.surface: A seer or prophet who foresees the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come to pass' suggests prophecy; in fact it means traffic approaching from behind to overtake you.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's reflecting glass shows the driver vehicles coming up from behind that may be about to overtake.

clue.text: Desperate Doctor Celsius visits wine town

indicators.note: visits here means calls round on, so the doctor and the Celsius letter go either side of the town

parts.note: Asti is the Piedmont town famous for its sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A desperate physician named Celsius pays a call to an Italian wine town.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor and Celsius read as one man, but they are two abbreviations that, on their visit, stand either side of the wine town.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate measures are extreme or drastic ones, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Party sends American from residence in defeated state

indicators.note: sends ... from means expels, so the American letters are taken out of the dwelling
from completes the instruction to send the letters out of the dwelling word

parts.note: a house is a residence
US is short for American, as in the US
a team that is down is beaten or in a defeated state

explanation.walkthrough: 'sends' and 'from' take US out of HOUSE, leaving HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively American folk gathering with square dancing is a kind of party.

clue.text: Play to defend unique wicket in stand

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these pieces go into the word for stand

parts.note: a stall is a market stand
one means single or unique, as in one of a kind
W is the cricket scoring abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A batsman plays defensively to protect a unique wicket during a partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman who stonewalls blocks every ball and makes no attempt to score, simply to avoid getting out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, batting purely defensively to block every ball is called by this verb; generally it means obstruct.

clue.text: Spoke more than once?

parts.note: looks like talking repeatedly, but spoke is a wheel's rod and the plural of the geometric term for that line is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone talking repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' reads as the past tense of speak; it is the noun, a wheel spoke, which is a radius, and 'more than once' asks for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheel spokes run from hub to rim like the lines from a circle's centre, so several spokes are plural radiuses.

clue.text: Friend frequents beach in Australia

indicators.note: frequents means is found in, so the word for friend lurks within the following words

explanation.surface: A mate who hangs out at a beach down under.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: 'plate' rhymes with mate, and the slang drops the rhyming word, leaving the porcelain word for a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang for mate gives this British colloquial word for a friend or pal.

clue.text: Something that restricts physical fitness

definitions.meaning: a proviso or stipulation that limits an agreement
the state of one's health, as when an athlete is in good shape

explanation.definitionFit: A stipulation limits a deal, and the same word names one's state of health or fitness.

clue.text: Girl made grand in swindle over small amount

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
a little is a small amount

explanation.walkthrough: Eliza in Shaw's Pygmalion and the musical My Fair Lady is a Cockney flower girl trained to pass as a grand lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's flower girl Eliza, coached in speech by Professor Higgins, is transformed into a society lady.

clue.text: Kid at home composed operetta

clue.text: High Church comment about blushing mother in retreat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for comment goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a note is a brief comment
someone blushing is red

indicators.note: in retreat means going backwards, so the word for mother is reversed

clue.text: Minoan daughter's song lifted finale

parts.note: a finale is the end

explanation.surface: A Cretan princess's song is raised to its climax.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the princess who helped Theseus escape the labyrinth was a child of King Minos of Crete.

clue.text: Given inducement, went in to get diamonds for monarch

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the word for diamonds replaces the royal letters

parts.note: entered means went in
ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the monarch; the substitution only works if the E after it goes too, the slip the editor admitted
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone lured into a jeweller's, swapping a crown for diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's slip: swapping ER for ICE in ENTERED gives eight letters; the spare E must also go. The Times editor acknowledged the error.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure with a reward, so someone given an inducement has been lured or tempted.

clue.text: In place that exhaust may become audible

indicators.note: becoming audible means spoken, so the word for exhaust is said aloud

parts.note: to wear out is to exhaust or tire

explanation.surface: A car exhaust that may start making noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like the car part, but it is the verb, to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: The relative adverb means 'in the place that', as in 'stay in place that you are'.

clue.text: Returned soldier to smallest room in White House

clue.text: Large ears to be reshaped — such treatment as benefits looker?

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: reshaped means given a new form, so the letters of ears are rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'looker' suggests an attractive person, but it means one who looks, whose eyesight benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: Laser eye surgery corrects sight, so this beam treatment benefits a person who looks.

clue.text: As dweller in 21 1 have internalised temperature, with instinctive knowledge
